1	---
     2	name: connection-discovery
     3	description: >
     4	  Find relationships between design parameters, populations and methods that no single
     5	  extraction states, and log them as typed rows. Cross-parameter links (a wheelchair's swept path
     6	  constrains turning space, corridor width and door approach), cross-population effects on one physical
     7	  parameter, compound interactions, and methodology findings. Modes: parameter (a determination or its
     8	  extractions), evidence (new extractions, gaps, pending connections), external (forward citations via
     9	  Scholar Gateway / PubMed), category-crosstest (every pair of parameters in a named cluster). Use after
    10	  citation mining, after a new or revised determination, or when a source bears on several parameters.
    11	  Do NOT use to audit existing connections. Absorbs connection-scout (D-0146).
    12	---
    13	
    14	# Connection Discovery
    15	
    16	**Model:** Opus-class or above (synthesis across dispersed evidence).
    17	**Output:** `connections` + `connection_targets` via `python3 scripts/db.py add-connection`, and typed edges
    18	between extractions via `relate-extraction` / `derive-extraction`.
    19	
    20	**Keyed on the parameter, not on a container.** The subject of a determination is a `base_parameters` row
    21	(owner 2026-08-26); the item layer is deleted (CLAUDE.md §7). Treat any `[A-Z]-NN` code you meet as prior-version
    22	content, never as a target. A connection points at parameters, slugs, identity-lens codes
    23	(`base_taxonomy_identity`), extractions, or a methodology, **one kind per column** (migration 120). Four of
    24	the five are foreign keys; `--methodology` names a methodological principle and is the one target kind with
    25	no table, so it is free text. The connection id is computed by the writer, never typed.
    26	
    27	## Two homes, and which holds what
    28	- **A typed edge between two extractions** is the strongest link: `extraction_relations` (`condition_on`,
    29	  `derived_from`, `delta_over`, `insufficient`, …) points from one figure to another row and can cross
    30	  parameters; across two *sources* it needs `--cross-source <reason>` or the writer refuses. When one parameter's figure is computed from or conditioned on another's, file the edge
    31	  (`derive-extraction`, `relate-extraction`); a `connections` row alone cannot be joined.
    32	- **A `connections` row** is the narrative index of a relationship. Its targets are typed rows in
    33	  `connection_targets` (`parameter_id`, `slug`, `identity_code`, `extraction_id`, `methodology`; exactly one set per
    34	  row), so a renamed or merged parameter cannot orphan a link and every target joins.
    35	
    36	## Modes
    37	| Mode | Trigger | Reads |
    38	|---|---|---|
    39	| `parameter` (default) | a determination written or revised | the parameter's live `specifications` row and its extractions |
    40	| `evidence` | new extractions, gap update | `source_value_extractions`, `gaps`, PENDING connections |
    41	| `external` | citation mining finished for a slug | T1–T2 forward citations in `evidence_sources` |
    42	| `category-crosstest` | a named cluster (parameters sharing a physical element, an envelope or a population; what a letter-category was) | every unordered pair in the cluster |
    43	
    44	`category-crosstest` is the exhaustive pass (`decisions/DR-2026-07-20-intra-category-cross-test.md`, ACCEPTED
    45	2026-07-21; "category" is now a named cluster of parameters): the other modes follow what an author thought to
    46	cross-reference, this one enumerates all pairs so none is skipped. A cluster has no table: name it in the GAP
    47	and in each connection's description. Per pair (per program) give one verdict, in words, because no column
    48	holds a verdict: the two are independent; one subsumes the other; they interact; they share a physical element
    49	under distinct programs; they are one variable conflated under two names; or they are in genuine conflict.
    50	Compare only within a measurement paradigm and device class (`measurement_paradigm`, `device_class`); a
    51	cross-paradigm pairing is a derivation, never an identity, and never a genuine conflict. Flag
    52	**cross-partition leakage** where a shared element or population links parameters across a cluster boundary.
    53	**Not built, and said so:** the DR's pair table (X6) and its hard gate on `stated` (X5). Until they exist a
    54	verdict has no typed home: "interact" and "shared element, distinct programs" are `connections` rows, a genuine
    55	conflict goes to `cross-population-conflict-mapper`, and the verdicts with no row (independent, subsumes,
    56	conflated) are named in a GAP for the cluster so the pass is not lost.
    57	
    58	---
    59	
    60	## Step 0 — Scope and dedup
    61	State the scope (a parameter, a slug or a cluster), what identifies it, and the mode. Load existing connections
    62	for the scope (`python3 scripts/db.py connections --status PENDING`, then join `connection_targets` on
    63	`parameter_id` or `slug` in a read-only query). A new connection with the same targets and `connection_type` as
    64	an existing one is a duplicate: `add-connection` refuses it, naming the existing id.
    65	
    66	## Step 1 — Read, by mode
    67	Read the live determination and every extraction for the parameter in full; for `evidence`, also open gaps
    68	(`db.py gaps --status OPEN`) and PENDING connections. For each extraction note its lens columns, so a population effect
    69	on a shared parameter is visible. For `external`, take T1–T2 sources from `evidence_sources`, follow forward citations,
    70	log mining with `db.py log-mining`; a cross-slug citation is a cross-parameter candidate.
    71	
    72	## Step 2 — Identify connections
    73	For each finding ask: does it imply a design relationship between two parameters, populations or methodological
    74	principles not already recorded?
    75	
    76	| Type (stored value) | Test |
    77	|---|---|
    78	| `CROSS-PARAMETER` | does evidence for parameter X constrain parameter Y? |
    79	| `CROSS-POPULATION` | does a finding for population A conflict with or reinforce one for B on the same parameter? |
    80	| `COMPOUND-INTERACTION` | would applying specifications X and Y to one person together give a non-additive result? |
    81	| `METHODOLOGY` | does it affect the guidebook's method? |
    82	
    83	Confidence is `connections.confidence`, read from the column's own CHECK (`HIGH`: direct evidence links the
    84	targets and the source says so; `MODERATE`: implied by reasoning or an evidence gap). A plausible relationship
    85	with no direct evidence is not a connection and the CHECK admits no value for it (migration 122): file it as a
    86	gap (`add-gap --category CR --priority P3 --description "speculative: …" --skill connection-discovery`).
    87	
    88	Route first: a relationship at MODERATE or above is a connection; an evidence or scope gap is a gap (`RP`,
    89	`AUDT` or `CONF`); a population conflict goes to `cross-population-conflict-mapper`; anything else is discarded.
    90	There is no connection-shaped gap category.
    91	
    92	## Step 3 — Log
    93	```bash
    94	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$SCRATCH/guidebook.db" python3 scripts/db.py add-connection \
    95	  --confidence HIGH --connection-type CROSS-PARAMETER \
    96	  --filed-in <slug> --source-skill connection-discovery \
    97	  --description "<one sentence: the relationship, its mechanism, why it matters to a determination>" \
    98	  --parameter 3 --parameter 12 --session <session>
    99	```
   100	The id is computed by the writer (omit `--con-id`; a typed one must equal `next-id connections`). `--filed-in`
   101	is a topic slug (`slugs.slug`, a foreign key). Targets are flags, each repeatable and each validated against
   102	its table: `--parameter`, `--target-slug`, `--identity`, `--extraction`, `--methodology`. The type sets the
   103	arity the writer holds: `CROSS-PARAMETER` and `COMPOUND-INTERACTION` need two or more `--parameter` targets,
   104	`CROSS-POPULATION` two or more `--identity` targets, `METHODOLOGY` one `--methodology`; a parameter target
   105	must be `active` (a merged or retired one is refused). Description bar: usable by the determination run
   106	without further lookup.
   107	Bad: "turning space and chair length are related". Good: "REF-xxxxx Table 2 gives a 1.35 m swept path for a
   108	powered chair; that exceeds the 1.2 m the turning-space figure assumes, so the turning figure needs its own row for
   109	that chair class."
   110	
   111	## Step 4 — Verify and hand on
   112	Count before and after: `python3 scripts/db.py connections --status PENDING` lists the rows (`--summary`
   113	groups them by confidence only), and the list should have grown by the number logged. Consumption: when a
   114	determination uses a connection, `db.py update-connection --con-id CON-NNNN --status CONSUMED --session …`
   115	(`--status` is `connections.status`, from the CHECK). A connection that reveals a conflict goes to
   116	`cross-population-conflict-mapper`; do not log the conflict here. `connections.opus_reviewed` exists and no
   117	verb sets it; do not claim a review that no row records.
   118	
   119	## Rules
   120	1. Never type a connection id: the writer computes it.
   121	2. HIGH confidence connections feed the determination run (`scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` stage).
   122	3. A relationship with no direct evidence is a CR gap, never a connection.
   123	4. No `[A-Z]-NN` target, no `--item-code`, no prefixed free-text target: use the typed flags.
   124	5. Use the CLI only; the archived registers (`gap_register.md`, `connection-register-active.md`, per-topic
   125	   `connections.md`) are not read or written.
   126	6. Feeds `cross-population-conflict-mapper`.

1	---
     2	name: cross-population-conflict-mapper
     3	description: >
     4	  Systematically identify and map where population-specific accessibility guidelines
     5	  produce opposing specifications when applied to the same space. Searches by
     6	  CONFLICT DOMAIN (environmental parameter) rather than population pair. Retrieves
     7	  resolution evidence from fragmented single-population literatures that do not
     8	  cross-reference each other. Outputs a conflict matrix with resolution status
     9	  and evidence quality. ALWAYS use this skill when: determining a parameter for a shared
    10	  space (Universal Mode or Tier 1); a determination run meets a parameter that more
    11	  than one population's evidence pulls in opposite directions; any
    12	  specification mentions "adjustable", "zoned", or "user-controlled" without documenting
    13	  which populations conflict. Trigger on: "cross-population conflict", "competing
    14	  access needs", "accommodation conflict", "which populations conflict here",
    15	  "do these specs oppose", "conflict matrix", "resolution evidence for conflict",
    16	  "opposing requirements", "conflicting disability needs". Phase 2B–3 skill.
    17	---
    18	
    19	**Model:** Sonnet-class (retrieval/collation) · Opus-class or above (resolution synthesis + best-practice determination)
    20	**Input:** Environmental parameter(s) (`base_parameters`), a determination under review, or a room type
    21	**Keyed on the parameter.** `conflicts.parameter_id` (migration 122) is the key and `add-conflict --parameter-id` is required; the domain label in the matrix below is prose that describes the parameter, not the key. The item layer is deleted (CLAUDE.md §7): treat any `[A-Z]-NN` code as prior-version content, never as a target. Population codes are `base_taxonomy_identity.identity_code`, and `add-conflict` **refuses** a `--pop-a` or `--pop-b` the table lacks (foreign keys, migration 121); the pair is unordered and the writer orders it. **The matrix below is prior-version content:** its population descriptors (`VIS`, `DBL`, `OFS`, `SENS`, `NEU`, `IntD`, `POTS`, `MCAS`, "fibro") are not identity codes, and most of its domains are not yet `base_parameters` rows. Derive the live codes (`select identity_code, display_name from base_taxonomy_identity`); choose the code whose name and description fit, and where none does, put the proposal to the owner. Never coin a code (OR-17). Which descriptors become codes, and whether the matrix stays as a seed list, is an open owner question (adjudication 2026-11-06).
    22	**Output:** Conflict domain matrix + resolution evidence register + unresolved gap flags
    23	**Chunk ceiling:** ≤3 conflict domains per run
    24	
    25	---
    26	
    27	## 1. Conflict Domains
    28	
    29	The finite set of environmental parameters where cross-population conflicts occur.
    30	Search by domain — not by population pair.
    31	
    32	| Domain | Parameter | Pop A need | Pop B need | Opposition |
    33	|---|---|---|---|---|
    34	| LIGHT-INT | Illuminance (lux) | DEM: bright circadian (≥300 lux task) | NDV/AUT, NEU, PAIN, OFS: dim, controllable (≤200 lux ambient) | Direct |
    35	| LIGHT-QUAL | Flicker, colour temp | NDV/AUT: no flicker, warm (≤3000K) | DEM: cool daylight simulation (≥4000K) | Direct |
    36	| VIS-COMPLEX | Signage density, pattern | DEM, IntD: high redundancy, pictograms, colour coding | NDV/SENS: minimal visual clutter, muted palette | Direct |
    37	| SPATIAL-OPEN | Sightlines, enclosure | DEAF: open, transparent, 360° visual reach | NDV/AUT: compartmentalised, enclosed, predictable | Direct |
    38	| ACOUSTIC-LVL | Background noise, amplification | DEAF: amplified speech, hearing loops, low reverberation | NDV/SENS, NEU: quiet, low stimulation, no amplification | Direct |
    39	| SURFACE-TEXT | Floor/path texture | VIS, DBL: tactile differentiation, detectable warnings | MOB: smooth traversal, minimal resistance | Partial (resolved: truncated dome sizing) |
    40	| MOVE-FREE | Autonomous movement | DEM: wandering, freedom of circulation | MOB (fall risk): supervised, contained paths | Partial |
    41	| CORRIDOR-W | Corridor/path width | DEAF: wide (≥2400 mm for signing pairs) | NDV/AUT: narrow (reduced sensory exposure) | Partial |
    42	| COLOUR-CONT | LRV contrast levels | VIS, DEM: high contrast (≥30 LRV diff) everywhere | NDV/SENS: muted, low contrast | Partial |
    43	| TEMP-RANGE | Temperature (°C) | OFS/POTS: cool (18–20°C); NEU/MS: cool (Uhthoff's) | PAIN/fibro: warm (22–24°C); MOB (spasticity): warm | Direct |
    44	| PREDICT | Spatial predictability | NDV/AUT, DEM: fixed layout, no reconfiguration | MOB: flexible, reconfigurable for equipment access | Tension |
    45	| FRAGRANCE | Chemical/olfactory | NDV/SENS, OFS/MCAS: zero fragrance | DEM (olfactory therapy): scented cues for orientation | Tension |
    46	
    47	---
    48	
    49	## 2. Execution Protocol
    50	
    51	### Step 1: Identify active domains
    52	
    53	From the input (determination, room type, or explicit domain list):
    54	- List all population codes the space must serve
    55	- For each domain in §1, check if ≥2 populations with opposing needs are present
    56	- Active domains = those with ≥1 opposition
    57	
    58	### Step 2: Search for resolution evidence
    59	
    60	For each active domain, search in this order:
    61	
    62	**Priority 1 — Existing project evidence:**
    63	- the parameter's extractions and live determination (`source_value_extractions`, `specifications`), read per lens column
    64	- SQLite `connections` table for PENDING connections: `python3 scripts/db.py connections --status PENDING`
    65	
    66	**Priority 2 — Aged care / dementia facility POEs:**
    67	Aged care populations co-occur DEM + MOB + VIS + DEAF by default.
    68	Search: `{domain parameter} dementia care facility evaluation conflict`
    69	
    70	**Priority 3 — Single-population design guidelines:**
    71	Retrieve opposing specifications from each population's guideline set.
    72	Key sources per population:
    73	- DEM: Dementia Services Development Centre (Stirling); HBN/HTM; Hogeweyk evaluations
    74	- DEAF: Gallaudet DeafSpace Guidelines (2010); PAS 6463:2022
    75	- NDV/AUT: ASPECTSS (Mostafa 2014); PAS 6463:2022; Enabling Spaces
    76	- VIS: RNIB guidance; ISO 21542; ADAAG detectable warnings
    77	- MOB: ISO 21542; BS 8300; ADAAG
    78	- OFS: limited — functional deficit research primary source
    79	- PAIN: limited — OT CPGs primary source
    80	
    81	**Priority 4 — Built project case studies:**
    82	Search: `{domain parameter} post-occupancy evaluation disability accommodation`
    83	Weight: dementia villages > neurodivergent housing > inclusive schools > public buildings
    84	
    85	### Step 3: Classify resolution status
    86	
    87	For each active conflict:
    88	
    89	| Status | Definition |
    90	|---|---|
    91	| RESOLVED-EVIDENCE | Published resolution with outcome data (e.g., truncated dome sizing) |
    92	| RESOLVED-CONSENSUS | Expert/standards consensus without outcome data (e.g., zoned lighting) |
    93	| PROPOSED | Resolution exists in guidelines but untested (e.g., adjustable everything) |
    94	| UNRESOLVED | No resolution found at population scale. Covers both "no resolution yet" and "irreconcilable here — requires individual co-design". Where it is the latter, say so in the CONF gap's description (what the OT assessment turns on); no column of `conflicts` holds the Person-Mode handoff |
    95	| CLOSED | Finished without an evidence resolution — the question was withdrawn, or infrastructure settled it |
    96	| DEFERRED | Deliberately not addressed this pass. Distinct from UNRESOLVED: nobody worked it |
    97	| ACTIVE | Live, in hand, not yet closed or resolved |
    98	| RETIRED | Removed from force without a successor |
    99	| SUPERSEDED | Replaced by a NAMED successor — distinct from RETIRED, which names none |
   100	
   101	### Step 4: Log to SQLite
   102	
   103	Do NOT write to `gap_register.md` or `connection-register.md` (both archived).
   104	All output goes to the tracking DB via db.py CLI.
   105	
   106	**For each conflict (all statuses):** log to the `conflicts` table:
   107	
   108	```bash
   109	# Get next CONF-ID
   110	python3 scripts/db.py next-id conflicts
   111	
   112	# Log conflict. The writer orders the pair; the id is computed when --conflict-id is omitted.
   113	python3 scripts/db.py add-conflict \
   114	  --parameter-id [base_parameters.parameter_id, active] \
   115	  --domain [the domain label, prose] \
   116	  --pop-a [identity_code] --pop-b [identity_code] \
   117	  --status [conflicts.status, from the CHECK: python3 scripts/db.py add-conflict --help] \
   118	  --resolution "[mechanism if resolved]" \
   119	  --evidence "[source citation if resolved]" \
   120	  --session [session-name]
   121	```
   122	One conflict per (parameter, pair): a second is refused, naming the first (`update-conflict` changes it).
   123	`update-conflict --gap-id` and `--status` are checked the same way; an unknown gap or conflict is refused by
   124	name. `python3 scripts/db.py conflicts --parameter-id N` reads the key back.
   125	
   126	**For UNRESOLVED conflicts only:** also log a gap, then link:
   127	
   128	```bash
   129	# Log gap first
   130	python3 scripts/db.py add-gap \
   131	  --category CONF \
   132	  --priority P1 \
   133	  --description "[domain]: [pop_a] vs [pop_b] — [why unresolved, what research is needed]" \
   134	  --skill cross-population-conflict-mapper \
   135	  --section "parameter [parameter_id]" \
   136	  --session [session-name]
   137	
   138	# Then update the conflict with gap_id (use GAP-NNN returned above)
   139	python3 scripts/db.py update-conflict \
   140	  --conflict-id CONF-XXXX \
   141	  --gap-id GAP-NNN \
   142	  --session [session-name]
   143	```
   144	
   145	**For RESOLVED conflicts:** no gap needed. The `conflicts` table record is the full output.
   146	
   147	**For multi-run sessions (>3 active domains):** the wrapper re-invokes conflict-mapper
   148	with already-resolved domains as context to skip. Query before each run:
   149	
   150	```bash
   151	python3 scripts/db.py conflicts --domain [domain] --summary
   152	```
   153	
   154	### Step 5: Output conflict matrix (inline)
   155	
   156	```markdown
   157	## Cross-Population Conflict Matrix — [scope]
   158	**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
   159	**Space / parameter:** [identifier, parameter_id]
   160	**Populations served:** [codes]
   161	
   162	### Active Conflicts
   163	
   164	| Domain | Pop A | Pop B | A spec | B spec | Resolution | Status | Evidence |
   165	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   166	| | | | | | | | ● ◐ ○ |
   167	
   168	### Resolution Evidence Register
   169	
   170	For each RESOLVED or PROPOSED conflict:
   171	- Source(s) with citation
   172	- Resolution mechanism
   173	- Outcome data (if any)
   174	- Guidebook implication (Universal Mode default, Tier 1 range, Tier 2 requirement)
   175	- CONF-ID logged
   176	
   177	### Unresolved Conflicts
   178	
   179	For each UNRESOLVED conflict:
   180	- CONF-ID (tracking DB)
   181	- GAP-ID (tracking DB, category CONF)
   182	- Populations affected
   183	- Specification implication
   184	- Research needed
   185	```
   186	
   187	---
   188	
   189	## 3. Resolution Patterns
   190	
   191	Known resolution archetypes (apply where evidence supports):
   192	
   193	| Pattern | Mechanism | Applicable when |
   194	|---|---|---|
   195	| **Zoning** | Spatial separation of conflicting parameters | Space is large enough to differentiate zones |
   196	| **Adjustable** | User-controlled parameter | Individual can operate controls; not DEM or IntD without support |
   197	| **Temporal** | Time-based alternation | Populations use space at different times |
   198	| **Graduated** | Transition zones between opposing states | Adjacent spaces with gradual parameter change |
   199	| **Layered** | Multiple modalities serving same function | Information via visual + tactile + auditory redundantly |
   200	| **Tier escalation** | Irreconcilable at Universal Mode; resolved at Tier 1–2 | Populations identified; co-design available |
   201	| **Dimensional** | Parameter optimised at intersection of acceptable ranges | Ranges overlap even if optima differ |
   202	
   203	**CRITICAL:** "Adjustable" is not a universal resolution. It fails when:
   204	- The user cannot operate controls (DEM late stage, IntD without support)
   205	- The parameter is shared ambient (you cannot dim lights for one person in an open room)
   206	- Adjustment requires disclosure of disability
   207	
   208	---
   209	
   210	## 4. Interdependencies
   211	
   212	**Feeds FROM:**
   213	- the determination run (a parameter whose evidence is population-contested)
   214	- `connection-discovery` (cross-population tensions discovered — replaces connection-scout)
   215	- `content-gap-analyzer` (population coverage revealing conflict)
   216	- `multilingual-research` / `functional-deficit-researcher` (population-specific evidence)
   217	
   218	**Feeds INTO:**
   219	- the determination run (`assess_cell.py`): a `contested` direction and the conflict matrix decide how a spread is shown
   220	- SQLite `conflicts` table (all conflicts via `db.py add-conflict`)
   221	- SQLite `gaps` table (UNRESOLVED only via `db.py add-gap --category CONF`)
   222	
   223	**Do NOT write to:**
   224	- `gap_register.md` (archived — use `db.py add-gap`)
   225	- `connection-register.md` (archived — use `db.py add-conflict`)
   226	- `references/connection-register-active.md` (archived)
   227	
   228	**Preceded by:** population-specific extractions for the parameter
   229	**Followed by:** the determination, with `set-parameter-direction contested` where the conflict is irreducible
   230	
   231	---
   232

-- 121_conflicts_typed.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- a conflict names its two populations by KEY, and the retired item column and the dedup index
-- that depended on it go.
--
-- WHY. conflicts.pop_a and pop_b were free text. The cross-population-conflict-mapper skill filed codes
-- (`VIS`, `DBL`, `OFS`) that base_taxonomy_identity, the identity lens every determination is keyed on, does not
-- hold; insert_conflict checked only that pop_a sorts before pop_b. Owner, 2026-11-06: "we do NOT want ... data
-- stored in the wrong cell"; "more columns = more specificity". Each is now a foreign key into
-- base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code), gap_id a foreign key into gaps, and pop_a < pop_b a CHECK rather than a
-- writer-only convention.
--
-- item_code is dropped: the item layer is deleted (CLAUDE.md section 7), add-conflict has refused the column
-- since the layer went, and no row can carry it. The unique index idx_conflicts_dedup was keyed on
-- (item_code, domain, pop_a, pop_b); with item_code always NULL, and SQLite treating NULLs as distinct, it
-- deduplicated nothing. It is replaced by a unique index on (domain, pop_a, pop_b), which does.
--
-- READERS: `db.py conflicts` and `add-conflict`/`update-conflict`; the conflict mapper's matrix; the render's

def close_adversarial_pass(pass_id: int, session: str, dry_run: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Close a pass (RC4). Refuses unless every lens has a row, at least one row is
    SURVIVED, every NOT-ATTACKED row's method says why, and every SURVIVED row's
    artefact resolves to at least one existing file under the repo.

    THE ARTEFACT IS PARSED, NOT MATCHED WHOLE (GAP-055). The antagonist brief asks for
    the artefact a claim was attacked WITH, and the antagonist writes it as a citation:
    "<file> page 15", "<file>; <file>", "<file> and the other five". The literal
    single-file check refused every one of those, so a good-faith pass could not close
    and nothing could amend a finding afterwards (the 2026-09-27 ruling forbids building
    that verb). The candidates are the whole string, then each path-shaped token
    (_artefact_path_tokens); one that resolves through dbcore.resolve_under to an
    existing file satisfies the finding. Containment is still checked on the RESOLVED
    path, so "../outside/x" is refused however it is wrapped. Path-shaped tokens that do
    not resolve are returned as `unresolved` (the CLI prints them as REPORTED): one real
    file admits the finding, and the others it cites stay visible rather than vanish.

    THE DATABASE IS NOT AN ARTEFACT OF ATTACK. A token that resolves only inside the
    directory holding the canonical database (dbcore.CANONICAL_DB's parent) proves that a
    file exists, not what a claim was attacked with: "data/guidebook.db <a query>" names
    every finding's subject at once. Such a finding still closes -- refusing it would
    re-open the GAP-055 trap for a good-faith citation -- but it is returned as
    `database_only` and the CLI prints it as REPORTED, so the weakness stays visible.

    PASSES THIS VERB MUST NOT BE USED ON. Pass 1 is held OPEN by the owner ruling of
    2026-09-27 (second, "exec 77 executed ...; further tooling on pass 1 stood down",
    references/project-standards.md), ACTION (2): "Do not build `amend-adversarial-finding`
    or otherwise chase pass 1 closed as its own effort; it stays open." Pass 2 was left
    OPEN by its own session (sessions/session_2026-09-28-research-batch-21-selection.md);
    the process-gap remediation plan the owner approved on 2026-10-01 says not to close it
    either, citing the same ruling -- which names only pass 1.
    Nothing here refuses them: a curated list of pass ids beside the passes table is what
    rule 8 forbids. The operator is the gate, and this is where they are told.
    """
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        prow = conn.execute(
            "SELECT pass_id, closed_at FROM adversarial_passes WHERE pass_id=?",
            [pass_id]).fetchone()
        if prow is None:
            raise Refusal(f"pass {pass_id}: no such pass.")
        if prow["closed_at"]:
            raise Refusal(f"pass {pass_id}: already closed at {prow['closed_at']}.")
        findings = conn.execute(
            "SELECT finding_id, lens, verdict, method, artefact FROM adversarial_findings "
            "WHERE pass_id=?", [pass_id]).fetchall()
        all_lenses = dbcore.check_values(conn, "adversarial_findings", "lens")
        missing = sorted(all_lenses - {f["lens"] for f in findings})
        if missing:
            raise Refusal(f"pass {pass_id}: no finding for lens(es) {missing}.")
        if not any(f["verdict"] == "SURVIVED" for f in findings):
            raise Refusal(
                f"pass {pass_id}: no SURVIVED row. A zero-finding pass must be able to "
                f"show what it attacked (2026-08-19 RULE), or it is indistinguishable "
                f"from a pass that never ran.")
        def _is_file(tok):
            p = dbcore.resolve_under(dbcore.REPO_ROOT, tok)
            return p is not None and p.is_file()

        db_dir = dbcore.CANONICAL_DB.resolve().parent

        def _in_db_dir(tok):
            p = dbcore.resolve_under(dbcore.REPO_ROOT, tok)
            return p is not None and db_dir in p.resolve().parents

        unresolved, database_only = {}, {}
        for f in findings:
            if (f["verdict"] == "NOT-ATTACKED"
                    and len((f["method"] or "").strip()) < 10):
                raise Refusal(
                    f"finding {f['finding_id']}: verdict=NOT-ATTACKED but method "
                    f"({f['method']!r}) is too short to say why. A placeholder is not "
                    f"a reason.")
            if f["verdict"] == "SURVIVED":
                artefact = (f["artefact"] or "").strip()
                path_tokens = _artefact_path_tokens(artefact)
                tried = ([artefact] if artefact else []) + [
                    t for t in path_tokens if t != artefact]
                if not any(_is_file(t) for t in tried):
                    raise Refusal(
                        f"finding {f['finding_id']}: verdict=SURVIVED names artefact "
                        f"{artefact!r}, and no candidate resolves to an existing file "
                        f"under the repo. Tried: {tried}. Lead the artefact with one "
                        f"repo-relative path to an existing (committed) file; anything "
                        f"after it is a qualifier.")
                missed = [t for t in path_tokens if not _is_file(t)]
                if missed:
                    unresolved[f["finding_id"]] = missed
                admitting = [t for t in tried if _is_file(t)]
                if admitting and all(_in_db_dir(t) for t in admitting):
                    database_only[f["finding_id"]] = admitting
        stamp = audit(session)
        conn.execute("UPDATE adversarial_passes SET closed_at=? WHERE pass_id=?",
                     [stamp["created_at"], pass_id])
        return {"pass_id": pass_id, "closed_at": stamp["created_at"], "findings": len(findings),

        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO search_execution_artefacts "
            "(exec_id, artefact, created_by_session, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
            [exec_id, artefact, session, ts])

def record_scan(data: dict, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Record one READING of one source against the parameter list (migration 103).

    The scan contract (catalogue-plan-v2 section 3; owner 2026-10-09: "Slugs guide our
    searches, but they do not guide what we derive and mine from sources!"): every
    admitted source is read against the whole catalogue, and each reading leaves this
    record, from which v_scan_ledger derives, for every (source, active parameter), in
    this precedence: EXTRACTED, STATED-ABSENT, READ-NOTHING-FOUND, READ-PARTIAL, BLOCKED
    (no reading, and a processing_blocked_reason saying the text could not be obtained or
    read), NOT-READ. A recorded reading always outranks a block.

    A BLOCK THIS READING PROVES LIFTED IS CLEARED. If the source's pairs read BLOCKED in
    the ledger before this row lands, processing_blocked_reason is set NULL in the same
    transaction and the result says `block_cleared: <old value>`: a reading of held bytes
    is the proof the obstacle is gone, and leaving the reason would be a false statement
    on the row.

    COMPUTED, NEVER TYPED (CLAUDE.md rule 8): `catalogue_version` is the highest
    parameter_id at call time (ids are never reissued, so it says exactly which parameters
    the reading could have covered), and pages read / pages total come from the file's
    own page markers (retrieval_log.page_coverage) and, for a text derived from a PDF,
    the PDF's page count.

    REFUSES: a typed catalogue version; an unknown or superseded source (a tombstone is
    never read again); a mode, scope or method outside the column's CHECK; a targeted
    reading with no target, or a target that is not active; a catalogue reading when no
    parameter exists; a --file-sha256 that is not a file the retrieval-log manifests hold
    for this source, or whose bytes on disk no longer hash to it; `full` over a PDF (what
    was read of a PDF is not knowable from the file: derive its text with
    scripts/research/full_text.py and read that), `full` over a text with fewer pages
    than the document it was derived from, and `full` over a text with NO page markers
    when the source's own logged bibliographic payload states a page range.

    A `full` CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST WHAT THE DOCUMENT IS, and the deposit is the only
    derivable statement of that (`retrieval_log.payload_page_range`): a landing page is a
    record about the document, not the document, and nothing here curates what one looks
    like. A source no deposit describes as paged (a code section's single page) keeps `full`
    over its single page.
    """
    if data.get("catalogue_version") is not None:
        raise Refusal(
            "record-scan: the catalogue version is COMPUTED, never typed -- it is the "
            "highest parameter_id when the reading is recorded (CLAUDE.md rule 8). A typed "
            "one could claim a reading covered parameters it never saw. Drop "
            "--catalogue-version. Nothing was written.")
    sha = (data.get("file_sha256") or "").strip().lower()
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", sha):
        raise Refusal("record-scan: --file-sha256 must be the full sha256 (64 hex "
                      "characters) of the saved file read, as the manifest records it.")
    mode = data.get("mode")
    target = data.get("target_parameter_id")
    retrieval_log = _retrieval_log()
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        ref = dbcore.fold_ref(data.get("ref_id"))
        src = conn.execute("SELECT ref_id, url FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id = ?",
                           (ref,)).fetchone()
        if src is None:
            raise Refusal(f"record-scan: {data.get('ref_id')!r} is not an admitted source.")
        _refuse_tombstone(conn, ref, "record-scan")
        for col, flag in (("mode", "--mode"), ("text_scope", "--text-scope"),
                          ("method", "--method")):
            dbcore.check_declared(conn, "source_scans", col, data.get(col),
                                  f"record-scan {flag}")
        top = conn.execute("SELECT MAX(parameter_id) FROM base_parameters").fetchone()[0]
        if top is None:
            raise Refusal("record-scan: base_parameters holds no rows, so there is no "
                          "catalogue to read a source against.")
        if mode == "targeted":
            if target is None:
                raise Refusal("record-scan: --mode targeted needs --target-parameter-id, "
                              "the one parameter this reading looked for.")
            prow = conn.execute("SELECT status FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id = ?",
                                (target,)).fetchone()
            if prow is None or prow["status"] != "active":
                raise Refusal(f"record-scan: --target-parameter-id {target} is "
                              f"{'not a parameter' if prow is None else prow['status']}; a "
                              f"reading is for an active parameter.")
        elif target is not None:
            raise Refusal("record-scan: --target-parameter-id is for --mode targeted; a "
                          "catalogue reading covers every active parameter up to the "
                          "catalogue version.")
        held = retrieval_log.artefacts_for_source(ref, src["url"])
        match = [h for h in held if (h["sha256"] or "").lower() == sha]
        if not match:
            listed = "; ".join(f"{h['artefact']} {(h['sha256'] or '?')[:16]} ({h['via']})"
                               for h in held) or "nothing"
            raise Refusal(
                f"record-scan: no file saved for {ref} has sha256 {sha[:16]}... The reading "
                f"must name bytes the retrieval-log holds FOR this source. Saved for it: "
                f"{listed}. Nothing was written.")
        h = next((m for m in match if m["exists"]), match[0])
        if not h["exists"]:
            raise Refusal(f"record-scan: {h['session']}/{h['artefact']} is in the manifest "
                          f"but not on disk. Nothing was written.")
        import hashlib                                            # noqa: E402
        if hashlib.sha256(h["path"].read_bytes()).hexdigest() != sha:
            raise Refusal(f"record-scan: {h['session']}/{h['artefact']} no longer hashes "
                          f"to its manifest sha256. Nothing was written.")
        pages_read, pages_total = retrieval_log.page_coverage(h["path"])
        if h["derived"] and h["derived_from"] and pages_read is not None:
            sd, srec = retrieval_log.find_fetched_artefact(
                h["derived_from"], prefer_dir=retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT / h["session"])
            if srec is not None and srec["artefact"].lower().endswith(".pdf"):
                held_pages = retrieval_log.pdf_page_count(sd / srec["artefact"])
                if held_pages:
                    pages_total = max(pages_total or 0, held_pages)
        scope = data.get("text_scope")
        if scope == "full":
            if not h["derived"]:
                # NOT ONLY A PDF. A fetched HTML page is a publisher's landing page as
                # often as it is the document (a repository record was recorded `full`
                # on 2026-11-06); what the whole document holds is knowable only from
                # the text full_text.py derives from it, whatever the fetched bytes were.
                raise Refusal(
                    f"record-scan: --text-scope full over a fetched file ({h['artefact']}"
                    f"{', %s pages' % pages_total if pages_total else ''}): what the whole "
                    f"document holds is not knowable from fetched bytes. Derive its text "
                    f"first -- python3 scripts/research/full_text.py --ref-id {ref} "
                    f"--session {session} -- and record the reading of that. Nothing was "
                    f"written.")
            if pages_read is not None and pages_total and pages_read < pages_total:
                raise Refusal(
                    f"record-scan: --text-scope full, but {h['artefact']} carries "
                    f"{pages_read} of {pages_total} pages. Record it as partial, or derive "
                    f"every page (scripts/research/full_text.py) and read that. Nothing "
                    f"was written.")
            _range = retrieval_log.payload_page_range(ref) if pages_read is None else None
            if _range:
                raise Refusal(
                    f"record-scan: --text-scope full over {h['artefact']}, which carries no "
                    f"page markers, but the source's logged bibliographic payload states pages "
                    f"{_range}: the document is paged and this text is not it (a landing page "
                    f"is a record about the document, not the document). Retrieve the document "
                    f"(R10; try the Internet Archive on a block, CLAUDE.md section 7), derive "
                    f"it with scripts/research/full_text.py, and record the reading of that; or "
                    f"record this reading as `abstract`/`partial`. Nothing was written.")
        # A reading of held bytes proves a block lifted. Read the ledger, never the class
        # list: v_scan_ledger is the one home of "the text could not be obtained or read".
        _blocked = conn.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM v_scan_ledger WHERE ref_id = ? AND status = 'BLOCKED' LIMIT 1",
            (ref,)).fetchone()
        _old_block = conn.execute(
            "SELECT processing_blocked_reason FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id = ?",
            (ref,)).fetchone()[0] if _blocked else None
        row = {"ref_id": ref, "mode": mode, "catalogue_version": top,
               "target_parameter_id": target, "text_scope": scope,
               "pages_read": pages_read, "pages_total": pages_total,
               "file_sha256": sha, "open_pass_done": 1 if data.get("open_pass_done") else 0,
               "method": data.get("method"),
               "notes": (data.get("notes") or "").strip() or None}
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "source_scans", session))
        cur = conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO source_scans ({','.join(row)}) "
                           f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})", list(row.values()))
        out = {"scan_id": cur.lastrowid, "ref_id": ref, "catalogue_version": top,
               "file": f"{h['session']}/{h['artefact']}", "pages_read": pages_read,
               "pages_total": pages_total, "text_scope": scope, "dry_run": dry_run}
        if _old_block:
            _st = audit(session)
            conn.execute("UPDATE evidence_sources SET processing_blocked_reason = NULL, "
                         "updated_at = ?, updated_by_session = ? WHERE ref_id = ?",
                         (_st["created_at"], _st["created_by_session"], ref))
            out["block_cleared"] = _old_block
        return out


def raise_follow_up(extraction_id: int, reason: str, warrant: str, session: str,
                    dry_run: bool = False):
    """Tag an extraction for a reviewer to re-check (migration 105).

    The owner's D1 answer, 2026-10-09: a figure from a source filed under another slug may
    set a published value, "but we still tag it for follow up later". Nothing can derive
    that a figure was read outside the purpose its source was admitted for (no
    slug-to-parameter map exists, and building one would be curation), so it is a
    judgement with a required warrant. The plan's caution stands: under the scan contract
    most whole-code figures are "from another slug", so tag only what a reviewer should
    re-check against the parameter's own literature, and say why.

    REFUSES: a reason outside the column's CHECK; a blank warrant; an unknown extraction;
    a second OPEN follow-up for the same (extraction, reason), naming the open one.
    """
    warrant = (warrant or "").strip()
    if not warrant:
        raise Refusal("raise-follow-up: --warrant is required: what a reviewer should "
                      "re-check, and why. A tag with no reason cannot be acted on.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "extraction_follow_ups", "reason", reason,
                              "raise-follow-up --reason")
        if not dbcore.exists(conn, "source_value_extractions", "extraction_id",
                             extraction_id):
            raise Refusal(f"raise-follow-up: extraction {extraction_id}: no such "
                          f"extraction.")
        prior = conn.execute(
            "SELECT follow_up_id, raised_by_session FROM extraction_follow_ups "
            "WHERE extraction_id = ? AND reason = ? AND resolved_at IS NULL",
            (extraction_id, reason)).fetchone()
        if prior:
            raise Refusal(f"raise-follow-up: extraction {extraction_id} already has open "
                          f"follow-up {prior[0]} ({reason}, raised by {prior[1]}). "
                          f"Nothing was written.")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        cur = conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO extraction_follow_ups (extraction_id, reason, warrant, raised_at, "
            "raised_by_session) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (extraction_id, reason, warrant, stamp, session))
        return {"follow_up_id": cur.lastrowid, "extraction_id": extraction_id,
                "reason": reason, "dry_run": dry_run}

-- 123_research_scope_and_ledger_precedence.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- two derived views corrected after the second operator walk-through of the run-pipeline skill,
-- 2026-11-06 (scratchpad run-pipeline-round2-adjudication.md, R2-1 and R2-3). No table, column or row changes.
--
-- 1. v_research_scope (new) -- the ONE home of "what is owed". Migration 122 added lang_jur_map.scope_status, NULL
--    meaning "not recorded". `db.py coverage` and v_coverage_priority then read the column in the wrong direction: on
--    2026-11-06 marking four languages `scoped-out` left every other row NULL, and `coverage` read required 0/0,
--    complete true. A NULL scope_status is OWED: an unrecorded scope never shrinks the requirement. The fill of the
--    column is a data migration after owner question 5 (the two jurisdiction homes), not this one.
--    Readers: v_coverage_priority, `db.py coverage`.
-- 2. v_coverage_priority -- reads v_research_scope instead of lang_jur_map, and compares the logged language folded
--    to upper case: live search_executions rows hold `en`, `fr`, `ja`, `nl` while the map holds `EN`, `FR`, ...
--    (derive: SELECT language, COUNT(*) FROM search_executions GROUP BY 1), so the anti-join never matched them.
-- 3. v_scan_ledger -- precedence corrected and BLOCKED narrowed. Migration 122 ranked BLOCKED above the readings, so
--    a reading of held bytes (which proves the block lifted) was masked by a stale reason. A recorded reading now
--    outranks a block, and only the reasons whose CHECK comment (migration 091) says the text could not be obtained or
--    read count as an obstacle. Readers: scan_debt.py, research_batch_dod R16-scan and R11-harvest,
--    verified_scan_integrity.py.

DROP VIEW v_coverage_priority;
DROP VIEW v_scan_ledger;

CREATE VIEW v_research_scope AS
-- v_research_scope: the (language, jurisdiction) pairs the research scope OWES a search for.
--
-- The ONE home of "what is owed": every lang_jur_map row not recorded `scoped-out`. A NULL scope_status is owed --
-- an unrecorded scope never shrinks the requirement (on 2026-11-06 marking four languages `scoped-out` left every
-- other row NULL, and `coverage` read required 0/0, complete true). The fill of scope_status is a data migration
-- after owner question 5; until then the requirement is the whole map, less what is recorded `scoped-out`.
-- Readers: v_coverage_priority, `db.py coverage`.
SELECT language, jurisdiction, role
  FROM lang_jur_map
 WHERE COALESCE(scope_status, 'in-scope') <> 'scoped-out';

CREATE VIEW v_coverage_priority AS
SELECT
    s.slug,
    ljm.jurisdiction,
    ljm.language,
    ljm.role,
    ( (CASE ljm.role WHEN 'PRIMARY' THEN 3 ELSE 1 END)
      + (CASE WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions se2
                    WHERE se2.slug = s.slug AND se2.deferred_reason IS NULL) = 0
              THEN 2 ELSE 0 END)
    ) AS priority_score,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions se3
     WHERE se3.slug = s.slug AND se3.deferred_reason IS NULL) AS slug_searches
FROM slugs s
JOIN v_research_scope ljm        -- CROSS JOIN: every in-scope slug x every owed (lang,jur)
WHERE s.status IN ('ACTIVE', 'STUB')
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM search_executions se
      WHERE se.slug = s.slug
        AND se.jurisdiction = ljm.jurisdiction

CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a non-absent extraction exists for the pair (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it.
--   5 BLOCKED            no reading covers the pair AND the source carries a
--                        processing_blocked_reason that says its text could not be obtained
--                        or read: nothing of it can be read, so the pair is not reading
--                        debt until the block clears.
--   6 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- A recorded reading ALWAYS outranks a block: a reading of held bytes proves the block
-- lifted (migration 122 ranked BLOCKED above the readings and masked them). A reading
-- COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >= parameter_id (the
-- parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that parameter. Rows 1 and
-- 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence than a reading recorded;
-- 3 wins over 4 because a full reading supersedes a partial one of the same source.
--
-- THE BLOCKED CASE BELOW IS THE ONE HOME of "the text could not be obtained or read": the
-- writers and gates read this view's status, never the column. It admits exactly the
-- processing_blocked_reason values whose CHECK comment (migration 091) names an obstacle to
-- the text: no-full-text, paywalled, no-doi, not-indexed, language. `no-quantified-claims`
-- and `superseded` are copies of typed facts (a recorded reading; superseded_by_ref_id) and
-- the writers refuse them by pointer. `out-of-scope` and `tier-not-required` say no text
-- was unobtainable, so they are treated as NULL (the source owes its reading) pending
-- owner question 8 of the round-2 adjudication.
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id, e.processing_blocked_reason
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id, pr.processing_blocked_reason,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent') THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent') THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         WHEN b.processing_blocked_reason IN
              ('no-full-text', 'paywalled', 'no-doi', 'not-indexed', 'language') THEN 'BLOCKED'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.scan_id = b.scan_id;

def _payload_bodies(pay, flag: str, why: str):
    """Every readable text body inside a persisted payload, for a bytes-not-memory check.

    FACTORED OUT 2026-09-13 so `set-icf-title` verifies an ICF title exactly the way
    `add-medical --icd11-payload` verifies an ICD-11 anchor. Two copies of a
    bytes-verification would be two places for the archive-member bug below to come back.

    READS ARCHIVE MEMBERS, NOT JUST RAW BYTES, and that is the whole reason this is more
    than `read_bytes()`. The first version of the ICD-11 check substring-matched the raw
    file, and the only artefact it will ever be pointed at is WHO's release file -- a
    DEFLATE-COMPRESSED ZIP in which no code occurs literally. Measured: b"MB56" in the raw
    zip -> False; in the decompressed member -> True. So the check refused the very payload
    that proved the anchor, and the ruling it enforced was unexecutable.
    """
    pay = Path(pay)
    if "retrieval-log" not in pay.parts:
        raise Refusal(f"{flag} {str(pay)!r} REFUSED: must live under retrieval-log/, which "
                      f"is the only store a later audit can diff against.")
    if not pay.exists():
        raise Refusal(f"{flag} {str(pay)!r} REFUSED: file does not exist. {why}.")
    bodies = [pay.read_bytes().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")]
    if zipfile.is_zipfile(pay):
        with zipfile.ZipFile(pay) as zf:
            for member in zf.namelist():
                # Bounded: a release file's members are text tabulations. A member larger
                # than 64 MiB is not what this check is for, and decompressing it blindly
                # is how a zip becomes a denial of service.
                if zf.getinfo(member).file_size <= 64 * 1024 * 1024:
                    bodies.append(zf.read(member).decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
    return bodies

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/audit/verified_scan_integrity.py — does every live extraction rest on a verified source and a reading?

WHY THIS EXISTS (CLAUDE.md section 8: what wrong thing reaches the guidebook). OR-11a
(owner, 2026-10-29): `extraction_status = 'verified'` requires a recorded FULL-scope
`source_scans` reading that covers the row's parameter; the write-time rules add that no
extraction exists for a source that is not VERIFIED, or for a (source, parameter) no reading
covers (contract criterion `verified-reading`). A figure stated over an unverified source, or
one nobody read, reaches a determination looking like any other. `db.py add-extraction` and
`amend-extraction` refuse each state at write time since 2026-11-06; this is the corpus-wide
reader for rows written before that and for any other path. Its readers: the re-reading
worklist (catalogue plan section 7, P3) and the adversarial pass.

EXAMINED is the number of live extraction rows (source not superseded, parameter active).
Three classes, each printed with its sources and its remedy:
  VERIFIED-WITHOUT-FULL-READING  the row is `verified` and no FULL-scope reading covers its
                                 (ref_id, parameter_id): record the reading (record-scan
                                 --text-scope full) or re-grade the row (amend-extraction)
  SOURCE-NOT-VERIFIED            the source's verification_status is not VERIFIED (NULL
                                 included): verify it (correct-source, or amend-source
                                 --field verification_status) or retire the row through the
                                 extraction writers
  NO-COVERING-READING            no source_scans row at ANY scope covers the pair (catalogue
                                 mode with catalogue_version >= parameter_id, or targeted at
                                 the parameter -- the rule v_scan_ledger states): record-scan
A row can sit in more than one class. FAIL when any class is non-empty.

ADVISORY, and red on main while the legacy rows stand (derive: run it). Re-grading them is
a data change, never a hand UPDATE.

Usage: python3 scripts/audit/verified_scan_integrity.py
Exit 0 every class empty; 1 otherwise; 2 cannot run.
"""
import os
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DB_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", REPO / "data" / "guidebook.db"))


def main():
    if not DB_PATH.exists():
        print(f"verified_scan_integrity: no database at {DB_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB_PATH}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    try:
        if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='source_scans'").fetchone():
            print("verified_scan_integrity: source_scans is absent (pre-103 schema)",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        cover = ("EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_scans s WHERE s.ref_id = x.ref_id{full} "
                 "AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= x.parameter_id) "
                 "  OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = x.parameter_id)))")
        rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT x.extraction_id, x.ref_id, x.parameter_id, "
            "  x.extraction_status = 'verified' AND NOT " + cover.format(full=" AND s.text_scope = 'full'") + ", "
            "  COALESCE(e.verification_status, '') <> 'VERIFIED', "
            "  NOT " + cover.format(full="") + " "
            "FROM source_value_extractions x "
            "JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = x.ref_id "
            "JOIN base_parameters p ON p.parameter_id = x.parameter_id "
            "WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL AND p.status = 'active' "
            "ORDER BY x.ref_id, x.parameter_id, x.extraction_id"
        ).fetchall()
    finally:
        conn.close()
    classes = (
        ("VERIFIED-WITHOUT-FULL-READING", 3,
         "record the full reading (scripts/research/full_text.py, then db.py record-scan "
         "--text-scope full) or re-grade the row (db.py amend-extraction --field extraction_status)"),
        ("SOURCE-NOT-VERIFIED", 4,
         "verify the source (db.py correct-source, or amend-source --field verification_status) "
         "or retire the row through the extraction writers"),
        ("NO-COVERING-READING", 5,
         "record the reading (db.py record-scan)"),
    )
    print("verified_scan_integrity — every live extraction rests on a VERIFIED source and a reading (OR-11a)")
    print(f"EXAMINED: {len(rows)}")
    if not rows:
        print("NOTHING-IN-SCOPE: no live extraction")
        return 0
    failed = 0
    for name, col, remedy in classes:
        bad = [r for r in rows if r[col]]
        print(f"  {name}: {len(bad)} row(s)")
        by_src = {}
        for r in bad:
            by_src.setdefault(r[1], []).append((r[2], r[0]))
        for ref, items in by_src.items():
            print(f"    {ref}: {len(items)} row(s) (parameter, extraction): "
                  f"{items[:8]}{' ...' if len(items) > 8 else ''}")
        if bad:
            failed += len(bad)
            print(f"    remedy: {remedy}")
    if not failed:
        print("PASS: every live extraction has a VERIFIED source and a covering reading")
        return 0
    print(f"FAIL: {failed} (row, class) pair(s) across {len(rows)} live extraction(s); "
          f"each class above names its remedy.")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# A canonical name may not state its own answer. This is the item-layer lesson as a
# refusal: `E-08 Corridor Clear Width (>=1200 mm Minimum)` biased every finding filed
# into it, because the container announced the determination before the evidence did.
# Measured 2026-09-09: no live terms.canonical_en contains any of these.
_VALUE_BEARING = re.compile(r"[0-9\u2265\u2264<>=]|\b(min|max|minimum|maximum)\b", re.I)
# Comparator WORDS are screened in NAMES only. A definition or description is ordinary
# English ("rather than reflection"), so it keeps `_VALUE_BEARING` (digits, symbols, min/max)
# and gains nothing; every NAME field uses `_VALUE_BEARING_NAME`.
_VALUE_BEARING_NAME = re.compile(
    _VALUE_BEARING.pattern + r"|\bthan\b|\bat (least|most)\b|\bno (more|less|fewer|greater)\b"
    r"|\bnot exceeding\b|\bexceed(s|ing)?\b", re.I)


def _name_tokens(name: str) -> frozenset:
    """The content tokens of a name, lower-cased, a trailing plural 's' dropped -- the
    one normalisation `_near_terms` compares on. 'Ramp runs' -> {ramp, run}."""
    canonical_en = (canonical_en or "").strip()
    rationale = (rationale or "").strip()
    if not canonical_en:
        raise Refusal("--canonical-en is required: a term is its name.")
    if not rationale:
        raise Refusal(
            "--rationale is required. Minting a term is an adjudication, and an "
            "adjudication that does not say why cannot be contested.")
    vb = _VALUE_BEARING_NAME.search(canonical_en)
    if vb:
        raise Refusal(
            f"--canonical-en {canonical_en!r} REFUSED: it carries a number, a comparator "
            f"or a min/max word ({vb.group(0)!r}), so it states a determination in its own name.\n"

- `adjudicate-term` for every observed phrase (`NOT-OURS` and `DEFERRED` are answers). `add-extraction` per stated
  figure: parameter, lens columns (identity, access need, ICF code+name, medical), value and unit, verbatim claim,
  locator, `--figure-role`, `--claim-type`, and `--relation` (**required**; `none` for an absolute figure); every
  vocabulary is in `add-extraction --help`. **The writer refuses:** a source not `VERIFIED`; a (source, parameter) no
  `source_scans` row covers (record the reading first); `--extraction-status verified` without a full-scope covering
  reading (OR-11a; `amend-extraction` the same); a numerical or range row with no locator — `--source-section`
  suffices below tier 4, the `--loc-*` hierarchy is required from tier 4 — unless `[UNVERIFIED-QUANT]` is in
  `--notes` (R3); `--verbatim-exempt` when a derived text or fetched page is held for the source; a byte-identical
  second row (a divergent reading is a contest, D-0168, and is written).
- `relate-extraction` for comparators (`--cross-source <reason>` makes a condition drawn from another document an
  explicit synthesis act; the quote verifies the from-source only), `derive-extraction` for computed figures,
  `raise-follow-up` for doubtful rows — its `--reason` vocabulary is the column's CHECK (one value today; a doubt it
  cannot name is a GAP until the owner extends it).

## 5. synthesis — read rows against each other
- For each parameter cluster ask which **other** parameters, populations or equipment change it (swept-path figures for
  different wheelchairs set different turning spaces, corridor widths, door approaches). File each dependency as a
  **typed edge between extractions** where one figure is computed from or conditioned on another, which may cross
  parameters (`derive-extraction`, `relate-extraction` with `condition_on` / `derived_from`), and as a `connections` row
  (`connection-discovery`) for the narrative: its targets are typed flags (`--parameter`, `--target-slug`,
  `--identity`, `--extraction`, `--methodology`); four are foreign keys, `--methodology` is a name with no table. The
  id is computed (omit `--con-id`); the type sets the arity the writer holds (`CROSS-PARAMETER` two or more
  parameters, `CROSS-POPULATION` two or more identities); a duplicate type + target set is refused; a merged or retired
  parameter is refused; `connections.confidence` admits `HIGH` and `MODERATE` only (migration 122) — a relationship
  with no direct evidence is a CR gap. `add-conflict --parameter-id` where populations pull opposite ways
  (`cross-population-conflict-mapper`; the pair is ordered by the writer). `connection-discovery` in
  `category-crosstest` mode (a prose mode, not a CLI) enumerates every pair in a cluster so none is skipped. An edge
  across two sources needs `--cross-source <reason>`.
- **Independence.** Sources sharing a root are one source. `v_value_independence` and `external_root_registry` hold few
  rows; where empty, trace shared roots from the citations by hand. `supersession-audit` → `add-supersession-check`.
- CLAUDE.md §6 reserves `best_practice_synthesis` to Opus-class models; no object of that name exists, so apply the
  floor to all prose you author at this stage [ASSUMPTION: its intended scope]. Reasoning documents need an attestation.

## 6. specification — the most accommodating value found, not the most common
- The state is **computed**: `python3 scripts/assess/assess_cell.py --db $S/guidebook.db --emit-sql <file>
  --parameter-id N --slug <slug> --identity|--icf|--needs|--medical <code> --session <STEM> --stamp <ISO instant>
  [--report-json <file>]` per cell on the scratch DB (it takes `--db`, not `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH`; it writes the convergence
  row and the determination together). **A cell** is a parameter × the lens codes given (`specifications`' unique
  row identity); today every lens of a parameter gathers the same extractions, and whether a lens should filter them
  is an open owner question. Do not hand-assign. Review its output against these tests; a failure is a gate or a
  GAP, never a hand edit. A re-run for the same cell is refused: `retire-specification` first.
  1. Name the **most accommodating** value found in practice, read by the parameter's direction. `contested` means no
     single value: show the spread with each population's direction. Frequency is never evidence; the steepest value a
     code allows is never highlighted. A cell with no direction stays `pending` and names `set-parameter-direction` in
     its gap.
  2. **Code is the weakest tier, not disqualified** (Option A, tier-system §8; ledger 2026-10-30, ratified). A
     determination resting on T4–T6 alone may be named, at the weak band **○**, with the code-derived flag and the
     convergence-not-evidence caveat, and is **never ●**. Read the report, not one flag: `regulatory_stratum_only` and
     `code_floor_only` are 1 on a code-only threshold with no direction; once an anchoring-tier finding supplies the
     direction the engine writes a proxy determination (`rests_on_proxy_inference` 1, `tier_basis` ending
     `(proxy_inference)`) and sets `regulatory_stratum_only` to 0, still at ○. Evidence that improves on it (academic
     research, clinical guidelines, advocacy and lived-experience work) replaces it and earns the stronger band. If
     the engine labels a code-only cell otherwise, that is an engine defect: tooling PR.
  3. The recorded rationale is the derivation (which sources, what they state, the rule version), not an endorsement.
- `raise-determination-gate` caps a cell at provisional.
- Checks: `scripts/validate_evidence_state.py`, `scripts/audit/derivation_handshake_integrity.py`,
  `scripts/audit/medical_lens_integrity.py`.

## 7. render — read from the database at render time; commit nothing generated

- **Citations:** APA, alphabetical by first author's last name, full author lists, DOI links, each with its "cited on"
  list, from `evidence_sources` and `evidence_source_authors` (`bibliography-compiler`). A field with no writer
  (stage 3) prints "not recorded". Provenance footer: schema version and database sha256.
- **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA is a precondition and wins over aesthetics; never self-certify, state only the tests run.
- **Sources of rows:** `v_best_practice` (the live `stated`/`provisional` determinations; it shows a code-only one at ○
  since migration 117, per OR-7) and `v_determination_provenance`. A `pending` cell is live (`retired_at IS NULL`) but
  not in `v_best_practice`, and stores no `governing_refs`. A view with 0 rows proves nothing; when no live
  specification exists the page can show only evidence and Gaps (contract section 7).
- **No check examines rendered output** (`register-invariants` has `check: null`): walk contract invariants I1–I6 by hand.

## 8. adversarial audit — a separate critic, then repair
`/adversarial` (the `antagonist` agent; never self-review). The critic's closing `json adversarial-findings` block,
the rule that its transcript is committed before the pass is recorded, and what "covered" means (a row per lens, at
least one `SURVIVED` row naming a committed artefact) are defined in `.claude/agents/antagonist.md` and
`.claude/commands/adversarial.md`: read both. Derive the lens set —
`python3 -c "import sys, sqlite3; sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts'); import dbcore; c = sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro', uri=True); print(sorted(dbcore.check_values(c, 'adversarial_findings', 'lens')))"`
— and assign each to a question, omitting none:
- **Accuracy:** stored bibliographic fields against the payload bytes, figures against locators, existence. L1, L2, S2.
- **Logic:** shared roots, tier, population fit, contrary evidence, frequency or code standing in for evidence,
  posture. L3–L7, L8 (was a zero-yield search well-formed), S1, S3.
- **Sequence:** every pointer resolves to an earlier stage's row; no extraction on an unadmitted or unverified source;
  no determination without direction and extractions; no stage verified after its consumer ran. `S4-sequence`.
`close-adversarial-pass` refuses nothing for a pass the owner holds open (pass 1 by the 2026-09-27 ruling, pass 2 by the
plan approved 2026-10-01): you are the gate. Then `/batch-done`. **`from-evidence` still faces its blocking gates:**
R17 (a logged search per admission), R1 (a Co-1/Co-2 search or source, or a reasoned `CO1-NOT-APPLICABLE` in a search's
`findings_note`) and R2 (`citation_mining` rows for admitted T1–T3 anchors). `scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py
--session <STEM>` scopes R2 and R17 to this session's admissions; for a source admitted by an earlier session they
examine nothing here, so run `--all` (measured against the ratcheting baseline) to see them. Mine the anchors; R10
fetches leave WebFetch ledger lines that `search_log_completeness` reads.

## Resume and exceptions
Resume from live state, not memory: `/orient`; unadjudicated observations (`observed_terms` with no
`term_adjudications` row); `scripts/audit/scan_debt.py`; open follow-ups (`extraction_follow_ups` with `resolved_at`
NULL); parameters with extractions and no live specification (`specifications` with `retired_at IS NULL`; "best
practice" is the `v_best_practice` subset); terms adjudicated `NAMES-NEW` that are neither a parameter nor declined
(`term_adjudications` left-joined to `base_parameters` and `parameter_declinations`). The scratch DB is disposable
and the canonical sha256 does not move until the migration applies, so a mid-batch failure costs only the unemitted
rows. A blocked source: Wayback, else admit UNVERIFIED with its `--processing-blocked-reason`. A zero-yield search is
a completed unit of work. Finish: `scripts/preflight.sh` once, `run_checks.py --selftest` after any rename, commit
scratchpad and transcripts (rule 6), open the PR last and `unsubscribe_pr_activity` at once (rule 9); research rows
and tooling ship in separate PRs (rule 10).

CREATE VIEW v_determination_provenance AS
SELECT s.specification_id,
       s.parameter_id,
       t.canonical_en                AS parameter_name,
       s.state,
       COALESCE(s.identity_code, s.icf_code, s.needs_code, s.medical_code) AS lens,
       l.role,
       l.exclusion_reason,
       x.extraction_id,
       x.figure_role,
       x.comparator,
       x.claimed_value,
       x.claimed_unit,
       x.claim_text,
       x.ref_id,
       e.tier,
       e.evidence_type,
       e.verification_status
  FROM specifications s
  JOIN specification_extraction_links l ON l.specification_id = s.specification_id
  JOIN source_value_extractions       x ON x.extraction_id    = l.extraction_id
  JOIN base_parameters                p ON p.parameter_id     = s.parameter_id
                                       AND p.status             = 'active'
  JOIN terms                          t ON t.term_id          = p.term_id
  LEFT JOIN evidence_sources          e ON e.ref_id           = x.ref_id
 WHERE s.retired_at IS NULL

---
name: run-pipeline
description: >
  Run the Accessible Built Environments pipeline end to end for a topic: research across languages and
  jurisdictions, evidence admission, judgment, synthesis, specification, render, then an adversarial audit
  of accuracy, logic and sequence. Variant `from-evidence` starts at evidence (sources already held, in
  hand or named by ref_id) and skips discovery searching only. ALWAYS use when asked to "run the pipeline",
  "research <slug> end to end", "process these sources through to specifications", "evidence and beyond", or
  "from evidence onward". Not for single-stage work: use the stage's own skill or `db.py` verb.
---
**Invocation.** `/run-pipeline <slug-or-topic>` runs everything. `/run-pipeline from-evidence <ref_ids | file | DOI list>`
starts at stage 3. A stage is finished when its verification passes, not when its rows are written. Re-entry is
normal (a new lead goes back to research, a new concept to base); record why, at the moment of return, in the
session record `sessions/<STEM>.md` (an attestation under `attestations/` goes with it, CLAUDE.md rule 2), and
commit it at the next natural break (rule 6). The database holds no marker for a return; the record and
`scratchpad/<STEM>/commands.jsonl` are the trace. `session-consolidator` is a prior-version procedure and is not
run. Derive every figure; paste no counts.

| Variant | Starts at | Skips |
|---|---|---|
| `full` (default) | stage 1 | nothing |
| `from-evidence` | stage 3 | discovery searching only; every later gate still applies |

**Open once:** `/session-open` first (it sets `CURRENT` before the first Bash call), then
`bash .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh`, then `/orient`. Work on a scratch DB (CLAUDE.md §4): `cp data/guidebook.db $S/guidebook.db`
and `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=$S/guidebook.db` inline on every call. This file orders the work; the research contract
(`governance/research-contract.yaml`, rule ids `R1`…`R17`, rendered by the SessionStart hook), CLAUDE.md §2 and
`governance/pipeline-contract.yaml` are the law. **`python3 scripts/db.py <verb> --help` is the one home of a verb's
flags and vocabularies** (rule 8: every `choices=` is read from the column's own CHECK); this file names only the flags
that carry a rule. If a verb or field you need does not exist, stop and file a GAP with `add-gap` (rule 10); never hand

```bash

  --scope {high_control|lower_control}   # clinical only; standard_eb takes

  #   REQUIRED since 2026-09-10: the tier is DERIVED from (evidence_type, scope) via
  #   schemas/tier_derivation.py, and --tier is now CHECKED against that derivation
  #   rather than believed. A tier with no type behind it is an assertion, and all 9
  #   sources admitted before this carry scope NULL for exactly that reason.
  --doi {doi} \
  --jurisdiction {jur} \
  --lang-detected {iso_639_1_code} \
  --lang-detection-method {native_title_verified|journal_family_inference|citing_document_language} \
  --slug {slug} \

  --session {session}
```

**`--ref-id` and `--local-ref-id` are not the same value, and this block said they were
until 2026-08-24.** It read `--ref-id {local_ref_id}`, which files the source under its
per-slug label: `evidence_sources.ref_id='RAP-04'`. There is no CHECK on that column, so
it inserts silently — and the row is then invisible to the `source_locators` high-water
mark, collides with the next slug that mints an `RAP-04`, and renders a citation keyed to
a label that means nothing outside one slug. `db.py add-source` now refuses a ref_id that
is not a global reference id, and names this confusion when it does.

  There is no allocator: `dbcore.next_ref_id(conn)` IS the rule — the high-water mark is the
  UNION of every table holding a ref_id, NOT `source_locators` alone (CLAUDE.md §4). Corrected
  2026-09-03: line 191 of this same file was swept on 2026-09-02 and this line, 24 lines below
  it, was not — so the file taught the superseded rule while citing the section that calls it
  wrong. Measured: `source_locators` tops out at REF-00970 and `evidence_sources` at REF-00978,
  so the old rule mints REF-00971, a live evidence row.
- `--local-ref-id` is the **per-slug label**, `RAP-04`, meaningful only inside `{slug}`.

`citation_mining` while `source_slug_links` held `RAP-06/09/10` for the same three
